questions.q: What typically pushes a training job from a single node to multiple nodes?
options: A single node can only run one GPU at a time
The model doesn't fit in the combined memory of one node's GPUs, or training would take too long without more total parallelism
PyTorch does not support more than 8 GPUs in any configuration
NCCL cannot operate within a single node
questions.explain: Jobs outgrow a single node when the model's memory needs exceed what fits on that node's GPUs combined, or when more parallelism (more GPUs, even across machines) is the only way to reduce training time further.

questions.q: What is "world size" in a multi-node distributed training job?
options: The number of nodes only, not counting GPUs
The total number of processes (GPUs) across every node combined
The amount of GPU memory available on a single node
The number of training epochs
questions.explain: World size refers to the total number of processes (one per GPU) across the entire distributed job, spanning all nodes — not just the GPU count on a single machine.

options: They are the same thing; the terms are interchangeable
Global rank is a process's unique ID across the entire job, while LOCAL_RANK is its GPU index on just its own node
Global rank only applies to the master node
LOCAL_RANK is used only in single-node setups and never appears in multi-node jobs
questions.explain: Global rank uniquely identifies a process across the whole distributed job (spanning all nodes), while LOCAL_RANK identifies which GPU on the current node that process is using.

questions.q: Why does inter-node communication typically become a bigger bottleneck than intra-node (NVLink) communication?
options: Inter-node networks like InfiniBand or Ethernet have significantly lower bandwidth and added latency compared to NVLink
NCCL cannot operate across multiple nodes at all
Inter-node communication does not use the all-reduce pattern
GPUs on different nodes cannot run CUDA kernels simultaneously
questions.explain: Within a node, NVLink provides hundreds of GB/s of bandwidth. Between nodes, communication crosses a network (InfiniBand or Ethernet) that is an order of magnitude slower and adds real latency from the network stack.

questions.q: What is "rendezvous" in the context of multi-node distributed training?
options: The final evaluation step after training completes
The mechanism by which processes on different nodes discover each other and agree on their ranks before training starts
A method for compressing gradients before transmission
The process of loading a saved model checkpoint
questions.explain: Rendezvous is how processes running on different nodes find each other and agree on their respective ranks and the world size before distributed training actually begins.
